title: The Parish of Saint Alder's
premise: Mara Villalobos, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made him both brilliant and isolated, is called to the drowned parish town of Saint Alder's when a body surfaces in the millpond wearing clothes stolen from his own apartment. The dead man is wearing a face Mara recognizes: Daniel Okafor, who supposedly died eleven years ago in the fire that closed Saint Alder's church and orphaned half its choir. As the statute of limitations on the old arson case expires in thirty days, Mara must reopen the fire everyone swore was settled, discovering that the parish's beloved priest orchestrated it as an insurance fraud that killed one child and erased another's identity. In the end, Mara exposes the surviving conspirators at a memorial service, chooses testimony over invisibility, and finally claims a place in the community he spent a lifetime observing from outside.
about_author: Noor Sandoval is a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine who spent nine years investigating suspicious losses before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for meticulous procedural detail and characters haunted by what they remember.

chapters.title: The Millpond Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Mara arrives in Saint Alder's to assess a routine drowning claim and instead finds the victim dressed in clothes he last saw hanging in his own closet. His photographic memory catalogs every detail of the scene, including a choir hymnal tucked in the man's jacket. POV: Mara. Beat: unease — the case has already chosen him.

chapters.title: A Face That Was Buried
chapters.summary: The coroner identifies the body as Daniel Okafor, declared dead in the 2013 Saint Alder's church fire. Mara remembers covering the claim years ago; the file was sealed by executive order. He realizes someone staged the drowning using his own belongings. POV: Mara. Beat: vertigo — the past is not past.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Mara learns the statute of limitations on the arson investigation expires in thirty days, after which the parish's settlement becomes untouchable. The local police chief, Ruth Calloway, warns him off with genuine fear rather than hostility. POV: Mara. Beat: stakes crystallize into a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Choir Loft
chapters.summary: Mara interviews former choir members, now adults scattered through town, and notices they all tell the fire story in identical words — rehearsed. One woman, Tess Ibarra, breaks pattern for a single sentence before catching herself. POV: Mara. Beat: suspicion — grief this uniform was manufactured.

chapters.title: What the Closet Gave Up
chapters.summary: Back home, Mara finds his apartment searched but nothing taken except one photograph: him at age twelve, standing outside Saint Alder's. He has no memory of ever being there, which terrifies a man who forgets nothing. POV: Mara. Beat: dread turned inward — his own memory has a hole.

chapters.title: Father Anselm's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the parish archive, Mara finds Father Anselm's financial ledger showing the church insured for triple its value weeks before the fire, with premiums paid by an anonymous donor. The donor's handwriting matches the hymnal inscription. POV: Mara. Beat: discovery — motive emerges from paper.

chapters.title: Tess, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Tess Ibarra agrees to talk if Mara meets her at the ruined church. She reveals the choir children were coached on their statements by Anselm himself, then flees when a car idles too long at the gate. POV: alternating Mara/Tess. Beat: fragile alliance formed and immediately threatened.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't Counted
chapters.summary: Mara pulls the fire marshal's casualty list and finds a discrepancy: eleven children escaped the choir loft, but the roster held twelve. The twelfth name was inked out. His own childhood records show a gap year in Saint Alder's county. POV: Mara. Beat: personal revelation — he may be the twelfth child.

chapters.title: Chief Calloway's Confession
chapters.summary: Calloway admits she signed off on the original ruling under pressure from the diocese and the insurer — Mara's own employer. She gives him the sealed evidence box she's kept for eleven years out of guilt. POV: Calloway. Beat: reluctant ally; the institution itself is implicated.

chapters.title: Smoke Memory
chapters.summary: Triggered by incense at a funeral Mass, Mara experiences a flood of recovered sensory memory: heat, a hand pulling him downstairs, a voice singing to keep the children calm. Someone died getting the others out. POV: Mara. Beat: emotional core — memory returns as trauma, not triumph.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Tess disappears; her car is found at the millpond. Mara suspects staging again, but this time the threat feels real. Searching her house, he finds letters proving she'd been blackmailing Anselm's successor, Monsignor Brandt, for years. POV: Mara. Beat: ally lost, moral complication — Tess was no innocent.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Monsignor Brandt offers Mara a quiet payout and the twelfth child's true identity in exchange for closing the file. He reveals the dead man wasn't Daniel Okafor at all — Okafor is alive, and has been hiding inside the parish all along. POV: Mara. Beat: temptation and reversal — the corpse had no name.

chapters.title: Okafor, Living
chapters.summary: Mara tracks Daniel Okafor to a boatyard two towns over. Okafor confesses he faked his death in the chaos, letting another boy be listed in his place — the boy who actually died helping everyone escape. He's been paying the parish hush money ever since. POV: Okafor. Beat: guilt embodied; survival's price made flesh.

chapters.title: The Name Under the Ink
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the inked-out roster line with baptismal records, Mara recovers the dead boy's real name: Mateo Villalobos. His own surname. The photograph from his closet shows them together. POV: Mara. Beat: devastating recognition — he survived because his cousin didn't.

chapters.title: Anselm's Last Sermon
chapters.summary: Mara finds Anselm alive in a care facility, dementia eroding him faster than any confession could. In lucid fragments he confirms the arson-for-insurance scheme and names the accomplice who set the actual fire: the sexton, still employed by the diocese. POV: Mara/Anselm. Beat: truth obtained but legally fragile.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Grounds
chapters.summary: Mara confronts the sexton, Hollis, among the graves he tends. Hollis admits setting the fire believing the loft was empty, and reveals Brandt ordered Tess silenced — she's alive, held at the parish retreat house. POV: Hollis. Beat: horror tempered by a chance to save Tess.

chapters.title: Retreat House
chapters.summary: Mara and Calloway raid the retreat house and free Tess, but Brandt escapes with the settlement documents and the evidence box's originals, planning to burn the parish archive that night. POV: alternating. Beat: rescue won, race begun — everything converges on fire again.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.summary: Brandt announces an eleventh-anniversary memorial service, packing the rebuilt chapel with townspeople as cover for destroying the archive. Mara realizes the congregation itself will be his only witnesses. POV: Mara. Beat: the trap inverted — publicity as weapon.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Anniversary
chapters.summary: During the service, Mara takes the lectern uninvited and, using his perfect recall, recites the children's rehearsed statements word for word, exposing their identical phrasing before the whole parish. Brandt moves to stop him; Calloway arrests him mid-processional. POV: Mara. Beat: climax — memory wielded publicly, invisibility abandoned.

chapters.title: Ash and Account
chapters.summary: In interrogation, Brandt unravels; the diocese settles, voiding the fraudulent claim and funding a proper memorial for Mateo. Okafor surrenders voluntarily, choosing accountability over another decade of hiding. POV: mixed. Beat: justice imperfect but real; each survivor pays or receives something owed.

chapters.title: Mateo's Stone
chapters.summary: The parish installs a headstone with the correct name. Mara stands before it and, for the first time, tells the gathered choir children who he is and why he came. Some forgive him; some cannot. POV: Mara. Beat: grief given form; belonging offered without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Photograph Restored
chapters.summary: Mara unpacks in a rented room above the bakery, keeping the recovered photograph of himself and Mateo on the windowsill. He accepts a standing consulting arrangement with Calloway and begins writing down what he remembers — all of it. POV: Mara. Beat: resolution — memory shared becomes belonging, and survival finally costs less than silence did.
